deep.reconstruction:
This folio is not by Riemann. It is page 1 of a letter dated Göttingen, 24 January 1876. Its author is H. A. Schwarz: the previous folio carries his signature and Weender Chaussee address, and this page continues the same correspondence in the same hand. The addressee ('Lieber College', with wife and children mentioned on the previous folio) is most likely Heinrich Weber, who was then editing Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876) with Dedekind. The subject is Hattendorff's posthumous redaction of Riemann's 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung' (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 13, 1867). 'Separatabdruck' refers to the offprint of that paper. The page has no derivations, only critical remarks on the text. In modern terms:

(1) Terminology. Schwarz objects to 'quadrirtes Linienelement' (squared line element) as careless wording; the intended object is ds^2.

(2) Formulas of the form log X = 2 log Y + f.c. Weber had conceded a 'small' inaccuracy here. 'f.c.' is probably shorthand for an added continuous or regular function or constant. A relation such as X ~ Y^2 near a point gives log X = 2 log Y only up to an additive regular term and a multiple of 2πi, which is presumably the imprecision meant. Schwarz blames Hattendorff, not Weber.

(3) The substantive objection concerns Riemann's argument on p. 25 of the offprint. The claim there is that, at a corner of the polygonal boundary with interior angle απ, 'the argument of Y changes by απ'. Schwarz asks how one knows that X - X0 can be expanded in powers of Y - Y0 at that point, when one is on the boundary and even at a corner of the domain. Rigorous justification needs analytic continuation across straight boundary segments, i.e. the reflection principle (Schwarz 1870). Even granting the expansion, a further inserted remark (only partly legible) says the conclusion still does not follow without additional work.

(4) Schwarz's proposed shortest justification, which continues on the next folio. Put a coordinate frame at the corner so that the tangent plane there is x = 0. Near the corner, orthogonal projection onto the yz-plane is approximately conformal. One may therefore take Y ≈ y + iz to leading order. The two boundary edges meeting at the corner project to rays enclosing angle απ, so arg Y jumps by απ as one passes the corner along the boundary.

(5) The next folio adds that the constant count requires all α < 1 in general, with exceptions only in special cases. It also says Riemann's explanation of the minimum on p. 34 is inexact.

No computation is carried out on the page; it is editorial and methodological criticism.
errors: No mathematical derivation on the page to check. Schwarz's criticism is substantively justified: expanding X - X0 in powers of Y - Y0 at a boundary corner is not automatic. It needs analytic continuation across the straight edges (the reflection principle), which Riemann's text does not supply.
Schwarz's heuristic Y ≈ y + iz near the corner is first-order only. It is correct for reading off the leading exponent / angle απ, but it is not itself a rigorous proof of the local expansion.

results.what: Local behaviour of a minimal surface at a corner of a polygonal boundary: the Gauss-map/Weierstrass-type variable Y changes argument by απ at a corner of angle απ; justified via approximate conformality of the projection to the tangent plane.
results.modern_name: Boundary regularity of minimal surfaces at polygon vertices; reflection principle; Weierstrass representation near corners
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1867, posthumous, ed. Hattendorff); rigorous treatment by H. A. Schwarz (1870s, reflection principle); later Garnier, Douglas, Radó

results.what: Constant count for Riemann's polygonal Plateau problem requires the angle parameters α < 1 in general (stated on next folio)
results.modern_name: Parameter count / non-degeneracy condition in the Riemann–Schwarz–Garnier treatment of the polygonal Plateau problem
results.usually_credited_to: Schwarz's critique of Riemann's posthumous memoir (1876 correspondence); later Garnier 1928

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a letter by H. A. Schwarz, not a Riemann manuscript. It is editorial correspondence on Hattendorff's edition of Riemann's minimal-surface memoir. The Schwarz–Weber/Hattendorff dispute over the 1876 Werke edition is documented history, and the mathematics is a known critique of a known Riemann argument.

checkable.asserts: Along the boundary, w**alpha with w going from positive to negative real axis through the upper half-plane changes argument by alpha*pi (shown for alpha=1/3).
log X = 2 log Y with X=Y**2 holds only modulo 2*pi*I (gives -2*pi*I here): a source of the 'small inaccuracy' in such equations.
Example: the image of the two boundary rays under w -> w**a encloses angle a*pi (=2*pi/3).

transcription_corrections: Author is H. A. Schwarz (letter), not Riemann; folio number '36' at the upper right.

In line 5 the insertion 'wie in dem vorliegenden Fall Herrn Hattendorff frei stand' sits above 'Ermessen des Herausgebers ganz frei steht', which is struck through; the transcription's structure is correct.
'f.c' after 2 log Y is an abbreviation whose exact reading is uncertain (possibly 'f.c.' = function/constant); the image shows 'f. c'.

The inserted line above 'Auch jetzt noch' reads roughly 'Und selbst wenn man dieses voraussetzt, ist man nicht des Probirens ...'. The last word is uncertain: the image suggests something like 'ungenügend' / 'überhoben'.
'Schwager' on the previous page is uncertain; addressee likely Heinrich Weber.
